description:
**The federation pressure test found eleven breaks and nothing carries them into the specs.** `MA-1` through `MA-11` came out of `53-multi-authority-scenario` — two authorities in one world, hunting the break the shared federation pattern has to survive. `51` (the ADR), `52` (the §-edits) and `53` (the scenario) all merged. The FOLD did not, and an 18-repo audit on 2026-08-25 found **no tasklist in any repo** owning it.

So the sequence stalled one step from the end: the question was raised, the pattern was designed, the pressure test ran and broke it in eleven places, and the specs still describe the pre-break design.

**This is why KINP sits at Candidate.** Its §11.1 federation edit is what demoted it, and MA-1/2/3/4 are recorded against it — the spec cannot be promoted while the breaks its own scenario found are unaddressed. KMI carries MA-5 as blocking for the same reason. The fold is therefore not housekeeping; it is the gate on two specs.

**Fold reactively, which is this repo's own rule.** The scenarios' standing policy is that an open question is folded *only when a pressure break forces it*, never speculatively. Eleven breaks are eleven forcings — but each one should be folded to the extent the break requires and no further. A fold that answers more than the break asked is how a contract accretes clauses nobody needed, and koine is a cross-organizational contract where that cost is paid by two companies.

**Some of the eleven may not need a clause at all.** A break that turns out to be a scenario error, or already covered by an existing clause read correctly, should be closed as such with the reasoning recorded. Eleven findings do not obligate eleven edits.

userStories.title: Each of the eleven breaks gets a disposition
acceptanceCriteria: MA-1 through MA-11 are each classified: FOLD (a clause changes), CLOSE (already covered, or the scenario was wrong — with the reasoning), or DEFER (genuinely reactive, waiting on a further break that has not happened).
The disposition table names, per break, which spec and which section it lands in. MA-1/2/3/4 are recorded against KINP and MA-5 against KMI; verify that rather than inheriting it.
A DEFER must say what future break would force it. 'Not now' without a trigger is how an open question becomes permanent.
This story produces the table and changes no clause. Deciding what to fold and folding it are different acts and conflating them is how a fold overreaches.
userStories.notes: Disposition table written as docs/reference/federation-fold-dispositions.md and linked from docs/README.md (repo rule: a doc not in that map does not exist). All 11 classified: 10 FOLD, 1 CLOSE (MA-11 — KCS §7 q1 already cites it by name as escape-hatch evidence), 0 whole-finding DEFER, 3 deferred remainders (DEFER-A/B/C) each with a stated forcing trigger. Attributions verified against each spec's own text rather than inherited: KINP §11 decision 1 + changelog records MA-1..MA-4 blocking AND MA-7; KMI §7.1 records MA-5 blocking + MA-10; KCB §3.1 records MA-6 blocking + MA-8/MA-9 — all three confirmed. Two corrections to the scenario's framing found by reading clauses: KMI §2 also has an optional `excerpt` (MA-5's field list is one short), and §3.1(d) already covers the differing-schema_id half of MA-9. No clause and no version changed. Guards: check-doc-integrity OK (49 files, 1036 links, 3 status tables match), check-tasklist-categories OK, .chief/verify.sh --run over the 3 changed files: all selected gates green (doc-links 0 dead vs 1 on main, retired 1 — fixed a pre-existing stale link in promotability.md to the retired task 84).

userStories.title: The folds land, minimally
acceptanceCriteria: Each FOLD is applied to the named spec section, to the extent the break requires and no further. koine is a contract two organizations implement; a clause added beyond the forcing is a cost paid twice.

Every touched spec gets a version bump, a Status reconsidered against its own ladder, and a changelog entry citing the MA-id and the scenario leg. A normative change re-enters validation — do not quietly leave a spec at its prior status.

Schema twins are updated where a fold has a schema shape, and the registry gets a note where a fold needs an immutable relation name. Never an in-place signature edit — that rule is already on the record.
The scenario is re-read against the folded specs and the breaks it no longer produces are marked resolved, with the ones that survive left visibly open.
userStories.notes: All 10 FOLD rows applied to the named sections; nothing beyond them. KINP 0.4.0 (minor — §3.4/§4.1/§4.2/§4.5/§5/§6, MA-1/2/3/4/7), KMI 0.3.5 (patch — §2 + §7.1(d)(e)(f), MA-5/MA-10), KCB 0.4.8 (patch — §2/§3/§3.1(b)(c)(d)(e)(f)/§5, MA-6/MA-8/MA-9), KGP Editorial only (no version, no new gate). Each spec got a version bump, a changelog entry citing the MA-ids and the scenario leg, and a Status reconsidered against its own ladder — all three deliberately STAY Candidate because a fold does not close its own gate, and each count is restated as a re-run against the folded text. Version choices are on the record: KMI 0.4.0 stays spent on the EDL removal and KCB 0.5.0 stays reserved for §2.2's removal (which 86's V-1..V-8 occupy), so both landed as patches on the 0.4.6/0.4.7 precedent. Schema twins: NO change needed and verified — no schemas/*.json models the KMI §2 asset envelope or a KINP equivalence link, and participant-self-description references the KCB manifest by pointer only (ADR-0007 d7); provenance.schema.json's $defs.license/$defs.egress are the vocabularies KMI reuses, not shapes altered. Registry: world_aligns_with ADDED as a new core relation (never a same_as signature edit — immutability rule). Scenario re-read: new 'Fold status' section walks all 11 against the folded text — MA-1..MA-10 no longer reproduce, MA-11 left visibly open by design, plus two honest residuals stated (MA-9's dedup key needs an optional schema_id; MA-3's two hashes are retained deliberately) and three DEFERs carried with triggers. Verification: node scripts/check-doc-integrity.mjs OK (49 files, 1067 links, 3 status tables match headers); check-schemas.mjs OK; check-registry.mjs OK (15 rows, 29 unique names); check-tasklist-categories.mjs OK (4 tasklists); .chief/verify.sh --run over all 13 changed files: all selected gates GREEN (doc-integrity, doc-links 0 dead vs 0 on main, registry) — 'all selected gates green — allowing merge'. Fourth mirror (CLAUDE.md Current state) updated by hand for all three versions plus the KGP no-move note. [Corrected on base integration, 2026-08-26: main independently landed KCB **0.4.8** (§4.3 autonomy posture, chief/71) while this branch was open, so this fold's control-plane half was renumbered to **KCB 0.4.9** throughout — spec header, status note, changelog, §3.1/§3 internal refs, the 3 checked mirrors, CLAUDE.md, ROADMAP, the disposition doc and the scenario. KCB now carries FIVE counts, not four; this fold still discharges only §3.1. KINP 0.4.0 and KMI 0.3.5 are unchanged. All four guards re-run green after the rebase.]

userStories.title: What the fold does to promotability is stated
acceptanceCriteria: For KINP and KMI, state plainly whether this fold clears the federation half of their promotion gate or whether something remains. These two specs are held at Candidate partly by these breaks and a reader should not have to infer the effect.
If a spec becomes promotable, hand off to `83-promote-kgp`'s promotability table rather than promoting from here — one place owns the ladder.
Coordinate with `86-fold-the-capability-versioning-breaks`: KCB's V-1…V-8 fold is the sibling of this one and the two must not contradict each other where federation and capability versioning meet.

Record what the pressure test taught about the FEDERATION PATTERN itself, not only about the clauses. Three specs independently deferred the same single-authority question and each promised it would 'likely resolve the same way' — whether that held is the finding worth keeping.
userStories.notes: AC1 — stated in the specs themselves, not only in a doc: KINP §11 decision 1 now says the fold clears NO part of its gate and that nothing else stands behind it (no second count, no outstanding fold, no koine-side deliverable), and a NEW KMI 0.3.5 status note says the same for KMI — the 0.3.4 note still read 'MA-5 (blocking) and MA-10 are open', which was stale after US-2. The answer for both is the same and is stated rather than inferable: the count CHANGED SHAPE (fold -> re-run against the folded text) rather than closing, so neither spec becomes promotable; KMI additionally cannot promote on a clean re-run because its count (ii) is KCB's work. AC2 — nothing promoted here. docs/reference/promotability.md (the ladder 83 owns) is where the effect landed: KINP/KMI/KCB rows rewritten, cheapest-first items 4/5/6 rewritten, 'Five counts as of 0.4.8' -> 0.4.9, and the 'On tasklist 53' paragraph's instruction to repoint the three status notes at 85 was REPLACED — 85 is finished too, so that pointer would have been stale on arrival; the rule recorded instead is point a gate at the artefact and name the owner separately. The re-run is recorded UNOWNED in promotability.md and in the ROADMAP F1 row. AC3 — the 86-coordination section is amended with three changes since US-1 wrote it: KCB is at 0.4.9 (main took 0.4.8 for §4.3 mid-branch) with 0.5.0 still reserved and unspent for 86; KCB now carries FIVE counts not three, of which 86 clears (ii) and only (ii), and KCB is promotable on neither fold because (iv)/(v) also fail the conformance gate; and §4.3's `effect` sits OUTSIDE the schema_id digest like `cost`/`volume`, which V-1's digest fold must not change. One near-miss named explicitly: MA-9's de-dup key is (provider KINP id, (name, version), schema_id) and `version` is exactly what V-4/V-5 are about — the folds agree ONLY because `version` is in the key, so 86 must not simplify it away. AC4 — new section 'What the pressure test taught about the pattern, not the clauses'. The prediction split: the DECISION held three-for-three (the scenario's own Not-deltas set — offline-first minting, byte-stable asset identity, route-by-lookup — each survived a direct attack, and no finding requires a redesign), while the APPLICATIONS broke in three different KINDS of way — KINP on meaning (5 deltas, 4 of the 6 blocking), KCB on carriage (3, 1 blocking; MA-8's own words: 'asserted, not mechanized'), KMI on decidability at the far holder (2, 1 blocking) — none findable by another plane's pass. Four further findings recorded: the shortest application (KINP, a §11 decision paragraph vs two lettered sections) took the worst damage, so length was not the variable and the keystone plane should be budgeted the deepest reading; a shared decision does not license parallel drafting (re-read each plane against its OWN surfaces, not its siblings'); the define-once rule is what let 7 of 11 cross-plane findings fold at exactly one spec each with KGP moving no version (~10 clauses instead of ~17); and the pattern needed one exception it did not predict (MA-7 — the prefix registry is deliberately NON-federated). DR-9 is recorded as the bound on all of it: domain B was a stand-in, so what needs an independently-operated far authority awaits a second adopter. VERIFICATION: node scripts/check-doc-integrity.mjs OK (51 markdown files, 1202 relative links, all 3 status tables match headers — KINP 0.4.0 / KMI 0.3.5 / KCB 0.4.9 candidate); check-schemas OK (9 schemas, 278 positions, 80 $refs, 3 fixtures); check-registry OK (15 rows, 29 unique names); check-tasklist-categories OK; `.chief/verify.sh --run` over 17 changed files -> 'all selected gates green — allowing merge', doc-links 0 dead vs 0 on main, verify-test 30 passed 0 failed. No clause and no version moved in this story.
